headline: Solar panels boost drought-stricken French corn yields by nearly 20%
meta_description: In drought-hit France, corn grown under rotating solar panels produced 19.6% more plant matter than open field crops, with plants reaching 79 inches tall.
summary_short: French farmers discovered that corn grown beneath 5,500 rotating solar panels thrived despite drought, outperforming traditional fields by nearly one-fifth.
body:
In drought-hit France, corn grown beneath 5,500 rotating solar panels produced 19.6% more plant matter than open field corn, with plants averaging 79 inches tall compared to 63 inches in traditional crops.

The elevated panels appear to have created favorable growing conditions even as the region faced water stress. By providing partial shade while allowing sunlight and moisture through, the solar infrastructure inadvertently became an asset rather than a competitor for the crops below.

This unexpected finding opens a new possibility for drought-vulnerable agricultural regions: agrivoltaic systems that simultaneously generate renewable energy and improve crop resilience. As extreme weather becomes more frequent, solutions that serve multiple purposes—feeding people while powering communities—may prove invaluable to European farmers.
quick_facts: 5,500 rotating solar panels installed over French cornfield
Corn under panels grew 19.6% more plant matter than open field
Solar-grown plants averaged 79 inches versus 63 inches tall
Test conducted in drought-hit region of France
